2026-11-18.title: Jindo County seeks in-home bathing providers
2026-11-18.summary: Jindo County reopened recruitment on November 17 for organizations to provide in-home bathing through its integrated community care program. Applicants must submit their materials in person to the county’s Integrated Care Team by November 23 at 6 p.m. local time.
2026-11-18.takeaway: Home-care equipment suppliers can use county notices like this to learn how Korea organizes local care delivery and which types of providers may be potential partners.

2026-11-18.title: Yeouido St. Mary’s and Soongsil expand clinical AI collaboration
2026-11-18.summary: Yeouido St. Mary’s Hospital said on November 17 that it signed a research cooperation agreement with Soongsil University’s AI-Bio Convergence Institute at a joint symposium on November 13. The symposium featured clinical research using large healthcare datasets and discussed future applications of AI in clinical medicine.
2026-11-18.takeaway: International clinical AI developers evaluating Korean validation partners can look to this hospital–university collaboration, although the announcement did not invite external applicants.

sources.label: The Catholic University of Korea announcement (Korean)

2026-11-18.title: Korea’s device regulator explains its innovative-device pathway
2026-11-18.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety announced a November 16 forum on how innovative medical devices are designated and reviewed, including examples involving digital medical devices. The agenda also covered health insurance and software cybersecurity; the announcement did not introduce a new approval or reimbursement rule.
2026-11-18.takeaway: International device makers can use the agenda to identify which questions to raise about designation, evidence requirements and reimbursement before planning a Korean launch.

sources.label: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety release (Korean)

2026-11-19.title: Anseong links home nurses with visiting doctors
2026-11-19.summary: South Korea’s health minister visited Anseong’s home nursing center on November 18 to review how it coordinates care with local clinics. The center, jointly operated by the city and the Korean Nurses Association since September, provides services such as wound care and medication management for older adults with limited mobility.
2026-11-19.takeaway: Home-care suppliers evaluating Korean partners can use Anseong’s model to understand how municipal programs, nurses and clinics divide responsibility for care at home.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare release (Korean)

2026-11-19.title: Korean study tests an MRI marker after transient ischemic attack
2026-11-19.summary: In a study published on November 18, a Korean team compared 329 consecutive patients with transient ischemic attack and negative diffusion-weighted MRI according to whether a separate contrast-enhanced MRI marker was present. Recurrent ischemic stroke was more common in the marker-positive group (13.3% versus 3.0%), but the marker did not independently predict recurrence after adjustment.
2026-11-19.takeaway: Imaging companies planning Korean validation studies can use this design as a reference for testing whether a new marker adds predictive value beyond existing risk measures.

2026-11-19.title: Korea outlines hospital AI pilots and payment plans
2026-11-19.summary: At a November 18 government forum, Seoul National University Hospital and Premier Partners signed an agreement to identify clinical needs and support investment in medical AI for regional, essential and public care. The health ministry discussed linking field pilots to its public-hospital AI network and reviewing reimbursement approaches, but did not announce a new payment rate.
2026-11-19.takeaway: International medical AI vendors can follow the hospital pilot plans while budgeting separately for reimbursement, which remains under development.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare release (Korean)

2026-11-20.title: Bonghwa launches home exercise visits
2026-11-20.summary: Bonghwa County began rolling out a program in November that sends physical therapists to the homes of integrated-care recipients with limited mobility. The county is working with the Gyeongbuk branch of the Korean Physical Therapy Association and a home-exercise association, and eligible residents include people who need community support after discharge.
2026-11-20.takeaway: Home-rehabilitation suppliers can look to the county’s delivery partners to learn what tools therapists can use during routine home visits.

sources.label: Joongdo Ilbo reporting on Bonghwa County’s announcement (Korean)

2026-11-20.title: Korean dietary screener shows uneven agreement
2026-11-20.summary: A cross-sectional study led by Seoul National University Bundang Hospital compared a food-group questionnaire with two 24-hour dietary recalls in 185 Korean adults. The methods placed participants in the same or an adjacent intake quartile 73.5% of the time on average, but agreement on sodium intake thresholds did not exceed chance.
2026-11-20.takeaway: Nutrition-app developers testing in Korea should validate each nutrient separately before using questionnaire results to flag intake risks.

2026-11-20.title: Korea issues two device usability guides
2026-11-20.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety issued two guides on November 18 to help manufacturers evaluate and document usability for good manufacturing practice reviews. The guides draw on IEC 62366-1 and provide examples for four device types, including pulse oximeters and single-use endoscopic biopsy instruments.
2026-11-20.takeaway: Manufacturers preparing for Korean review can use the examples to check their usability test plans and reports without treating the guidance as a new approval rule.

sources.label: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety release (Korean)

2026-11-21.title: Incheon’s Yeonsu District staffs all 15 neighborhoods for integrated care
2026-11-21.summary: Yeonsu District said it had assigned dedicated integrated-care staff to all 15 neighborhood welfare centers to identify residents who need help and connect them with medical, long-term care and other support services. Four regional groups, involving the district, public health centers and the National Health Insurance Service, have been reviewing individual cases since September.
2026-11-21.takeaway: Home-care companies can use Yeonsu’s setup to identify who handles referrals and where a service or tool might fit into the local care process.

2026-11-21.title: Korean study evaluates a driving self-assessment app for older adults
2026-11-21.summary: Kangwon National University researchers analyzed smartphone self-assessments from 610 Korean adults aged 65 or older in a cross-sectional study using data collected in 2018 and 2019. Lower scores for vehicle control and vision were associated with having stopped driving, while lower scores in several thinking and health domains were associated with self-reported recent crashes.
2026-11-21.takeaway: Developers of driving-assessment tools can use the results to choose what to test with Korean partners, but need prospective data before claiming the tool predicts crashes.

2026-11-21.title: National Cancer Center posts draft specifications for accessible kiosks
2026-11-21.summary: South Korea’s National Cancer Center published draft procurement specifications on November 20 for accessible kiosks that support outpatient check-in and basic measurements. The notice is a pre-tender disclosure, not confirmation of a purchase, contract award or installation.
2026-11-21.takeaway: International kiosk and measurement-system suppliers can track the eventual tender to see how a Korean public hospital combines accessibility, check-in and routine measurements.

sources.label: National Cancer Center procurement notice list (Korean)

2026-11-22.title: Korea publishes proposals for its first five-year integrated care plan
2026-11-22.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Health and Welfare released hearing materials on November 20 for its draft 2026–2030 integrated community care plan. The underlying research examined ways to expand eligibility and services and narrow regional gaps, but the ministry said the plan would be finalized only after further consultation and review.
2026-11-22.takeaway: Home-care companies can use the proposals to identify potential areas for local collaboration, without treating them as funded programs or procurement notices.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare hearing materials (Korean)
Ministry of Health and Welfare release (Korean)

2026-11-22.title: Wearable study tracks sleep across Korean hospital shifts
2026-11-22.summary: In an exploratory study published November 21, 30 nurses at one South Korean hospital wore sleep-tracking rings and completed daily surveys for at least 28 days. Their recorded sleep was shorter after night shifts than after day or evening shifts, and sleep on days off varied with the surrounding work schedule.
2026-11-22.takeaway: Wearable developers planning Korean hospital studies can use this design to evaluate how shift sequences affect measurements rather than grouping participants by shift type alone.

2026-11-22.title: Korea revises medical device spending disclosures
2026-11-22.summary: A South Korean medical device distribution rule took effect on November 20, revising disclosures of financial benefits provided to healthcare professionals and institutions. The updated reporting form and disclosure-timing provision apply from the following fiscal year, and the form calls for recording transaction amounts before payment-term discounts.
2026-11-22.takeaway: International device makers can check with Korean sales partners whether their systems capture pre-discount amounts for the applicable reporting period.

2026-11-23.title: Gumi recruits local integrated-care providers
2026-11-23.summary: Gumi posted a call on November 23 for organizations to deliver services under its local Gumi Baro Care program. Providers must apply in person between December 3 and December 7, with applications closing at 18:00 Korea time on the final day.
2026-11-23.takeaway: For overseas companies, the recruitment identifies Gumi’s Integrated Care Team as a starting point for learning which local service operators could be implementation partners.

2026-11-23.title: Korean study tracks mobility in a community walking program
2026-11-23.summary: A Korean university team conducted a 10-week nonrandomized controlled study with 30 adults aged 60 to 79, of whom 25 completed follow-up. Two-minute step counts rose in the supervised barefoot-walking group and fell in the usual-lifestyle group, but the study did not compare the program with walking in shoes.
2026-11-23.takeaway: Companies testing mobility products with Korean community partners can consider this team’s field-testing approach and use an active comparison group to distinguish product effects from exercise effects.

2026-11-23.title: NHIS Ilsan Hospital reopens medical equipment tender
2026-11-23.summary: National Health Insurance Service Ilsan Hospital reissued a restricted competitive tender on November 20 for four units across three categories of medical equipment. The hospital will review technical eligibility before opening price bids, with submissions due November 26 at 10:00 Korea time.
2026-11-23.takeaway: Suppliers considering this procurement should review the hospital’s technical specifications and bidder eligibility with a Korean partner before pricing a bid.

2026-11-24.title: Ganghwa County plans to expand home-based care
2026-11-24.summary: Ganghwa County said on November 23 that its integrated care program had reached 250 people in its first year, with services including home exercise visits and transitional housing after discharge. The county plans to add hospital caregiver-cost assistance, adult incontinence supplies and a home safety monitoring service in 2027.
2026-11-24.takeaway: Overseas home-care companies can use the county’s plans to identify where local providers may need monitoring or rehabilitation tools for use outside hospitals.

2026-11-24.title: Hanyang team tests wrist pulse data for vascular age estimation
2026-11-24.summary: Researchers at Hanyang University and its Guri Hospital used simulated training data and existing human recordings to test a model that estimates vascular age from a wrist artery waveform and blood pressure. Mean absolute error against chronological age was about seven years in two cohorts with normal blood pressure, and the study did not test whether the estimates predict cardiovascular events.
2026-11-24.takeaway: Cardiovascular device developers could approach the team about prospectively validating the model with noninvasive sensors and clinical outcomes.

2026-11-24.title: Dongwoon Anatech reports digital-device GMP milestone
2026-11-24.summary: Dongwoon Anatech said it received Korea’s digital medical device manufacturing quality certificate for its D-SaLife saliva glucose monitoring system on November 23, after the regulator issued it on November 5. The certificate does not authorize the product for sale, and the company said clinical trials and other regulatory steps remain.
2026-11-24.takeaway: Overseas developers of software-enabled diagnostics should plan for manufacturing quality compliance separately from clinical evidence and product authorization.

2026-11-25.title: Goryeong reviews home exercise for its 2027 care plan
2026-11-25.summary: On November 24, Goryeong County listed a public consultation on its draft 2027 integrated care plan. The county’s care council reviewed the draft, which proposes home exercise visits, balanced meals and closer coordination with local medical providers.
2026-11-25.takeaway: Companies offering home exercise or nutrition services can track the consultation for a clearer picture of what the county plans to deliver with local partners.

2026-11-25.title: Korean pilot tests electroacupuncture for radiating leg pain
2026-11-25.summary: A Korean research team randomized 45 patients with lumbar radicular leg pain to six weeks of electroacupuncture or a sham procedure and assessed pain and brain activity before and after treatment. The electroacupuncture group had an adjusted 1.49-point greater reduction in leg pain, but whether the observed changes in brain connectivity explained symptom improvement remains unclear.
2026-11-25.takeaway: Developers of non-drug pain devices can use the study as a reference for designing sham controls and pairing patient-reported outcomes with imaging in a Korean pilot.

sources.label: BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies: original study

2026-11-25.title: Yangsan hospital reopens blood cell separator tender
2026-11-25.summary: Pusan National University Yangsan Hospital reopened bidding for one automated blood cell separator and its installation, with a contract estimate of KRW 176 million including VAT. Bids close at 10:00 a.m. Korea time on November 30, and the specification calls for continuous-flow operation for uses including therapeutic plasma exchange and cell collection.
2026-11-25.takeaway: Overseas suppliers should check whether a Korean distributor meets the tender’s product registration, medical-device business and small-business eligibility requirements.

sources.label: KONEPS: official rebid notice and specifications (ZIP)

2026-11-26.title: Korea seeks an operator for older adults’ knee surgery support
2026-11-26.summary: On November 25, the Ministry of Health and Welfare opened a call for an organization to run the 2027 knee replacement surgery support program for older adults. The call is part of the ministry’s older-adult health program and accepts applications through December 10.
2026-11-26.takeaway: Orthopedic and rehabilitation companies can track the operator selection to identify which organization will coordinate this publicly supported pathway to surgery.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare: operator call

2026-11-26.title: Hongik study finds barriers in mobile public services for older adults
2026-11-26.summary: A Hongik University-led study asked 35 adults aged 20–29 and 30 adults aged 69–91 to attempt three Gov24 certificate workflows on their own phones. The younger group completed every attempt, compared with completion rates of 17%, 3% and 3% across the three workflows in the older group.
2026-11-26.takeaway: Companies building digital health services for Korea can use the study’s approach to test whether older adults can complete an entire workflow, including authentication and handoffs, without help.

2026-11-26.title: National Cancer Center reopens cardiac monitor tender
2026-11-26.summary: Korea’s National Cancer Center reopened bidding on November 25 for two thermodilution cardiac output monitors under general competition, with a total budget of KRW 40 million including VAT. Bids close on December 1 at 11:00 Korea time, and the center reviews technical specifications before opening price bids.
2026-11-26.takeaway: Overseas monitor makers should confirm that a Korean supplier can document local device authorization and submit the required technical materials as well as the electronic bid.

sources.label: KONEPS: National Cancer Center tender notice (PDF)
